overall: The AG found one board member individually violated the Open Meeting Law by emailing a quorum on November 17, and the Board violated the law by approving four executive session minutes late; other allegations were rejected or declined.

allegations.summary: A board member alleged the Board discussed reinstating the Town Administrator at an October 6 meeting although the topic was not on the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board's discussion during the October 6 meeting of reinstating the Town Administrator did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A board member alleged the Board broke its own 48-hour agenda-addition rule and that the meeting was biased by supporters of the Town Administrator.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, these allegations would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25. Accordingly, we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: A board member alleged the Board deliberated by email on October 14 about scheduling a meeting on sexual harassment allegations.
allegations.key_passage: We find that these emails were merely administrative in nature regarding the scheduling of a meeting, fitting squarely within the Open Meeting Law's exception to the definition of deliberation.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged a board member individually deliberated by email on November 17; the AG found improper deliberation but declined to find it intentional.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that Member Weingold individually violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A resident alleged the Board failed to timely approve several sets of executive session minutes; the Board conceded the delay for four sessions.
allegations.key_passage: The Board concedes that it did not approve minutes for executive sessions that took place on July 21, October 4, November 4, and November 17, in a timely manner.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law by the Board.
Publicly release Member Weingold's November 17 email within 30 days of the Board's receipt of the letter.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
